arguments.value: 5-year-old female greyhound referred for bilateral Dioctophyme renale infection with severe azotemia/uremic syndrome and non-oliguric stage 5 AKI, confirmed by ultrasound and urinalysis showing D. renale eggs, hematuria, proteinuria, and leukocyturia; underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy and bilateral nephroscopy for removal of multiple renal parasites, with postoperative renal recovery and discharge with CKD stage 3 and proteinuria/prehypertension.
